Hi Sergio — draft sketches below (assumptions noted). I attached our capacity pricelist for reference.

Assumptions (for all sketches): mid = 8M tokens/month; high = 20M tokens/month; avg tokens per request ~400 total (in+out).

1) Hosted API (fastest to go live)
- Pricing: input $0.00050/token, output $0.00100/token (sample public tier).
- Estimates: mid = (8M * average blended rate $0.0009) ≈ $7,200/month; high ≈ $18,000/month.
- Notes: No infra commit or platform fee; includes multiregion failover; predictable per-token spend but can be higher at scale.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — recommended for predictable latency/cost
- Pricing: Reserved commit covers baseline capacity (example: 4x high-util GPUs) at $16,000/month for baseline throughput that covers ~120 QPS with our batching optimizations. Overage tokens billed at a discounted per-token equivalent ~$0.00025/token.
- Estimates: mid = reserved $16,000 + small overage estimate ≈ $16,500/month (net cheaper than hosted at scale); high (20M) ≈ $18,000–$20,000/month depending on burst profile.
- Notes: SLA-backed latency targets, prefix/KV cache reduces token execution for repeat queries; best for heavy, stable traffic.

3) Private VPC / On-prem
- Pricing: One-time private deployment platform fee (example) $25,000 + monthly platform support $4,000. Infra (customer or Redwoods-managed) depends on instance types; rough infra estimate for equivalent capacity ≈ $12,000/month.
- Estimates: month 1 = $25,000 + $12,000 = $37,000 (plus support); ongoing ≈ $16,000/month including platform & infra.
- Notes: Best for strict compliance and data residency; longer procurement lead time and one-time onboarding work.

Recommendation & next step: Given BrightLeafs expected QPS and likely HIPAA need, Id recommend we position Dedicated as the primary option (predictable latency and overall lower unit cost) and present Hosted as a lower-friction pilot path. Private VPC is available if procurement requires it, but we should surface the upfront integration fee early.

If that looks good I can convert this into a 1-page summary to share with procurement and schedule a 30-min call with BrightLeaf this week.

Quick technical notes to pair with Marissa's pricing sketch: 
- Feasibility: 120 QPS with ~400 tokens/session is feasible on Dedicated with 4 GPU nodes if we enable continuous batching and prefix caching; p95 < 400ms is achievable in that config for most requests.
- Cost reduction levers: KV/prefix cache (20–30% token reduction on repeat requests), mixed-precision/INT8 quantization for model weights (reduces memory pressure and lets us run higher throughput on the same hardware but can impact generation quality slightly — needs eval).
- Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted gives fast launch and no ops lift; Dedicated gives deterministic tail latency and better unit economics at scale due to reserved pricing and local caching.
- Private VPC: Network egress and maintenance windows are the main operational items to plan for. We can run our control plane in the cloud and customer VPC for data plane to minimize egress but that changes the pricing model.
- Pilot approach: Start Hosted (2–4 week pilot) to validate traffic patterns and prompts, then flip to Dedicated reserved commit in Q2 if usage justifies it. We can offer a short trial of reserved capacity to accelerate that decision.

Happy to join the procurement call and help size exact GPU SKU counts once BrightLeaf confirms average tokens and a 3-month usage curve.
